ownerDecision.request: Keep all our new designs and make these new tanks. Yes—the earlier T-90SM-based designs.
ownerDecision.scope: Preserve all twelve current national modernization models. Add separate Hetman II and Zubr II concepts carrying the earlier broad welded turret and long bustle lineage, with independently authored national turret shapes, surrounding armor, roof equipment and thick fitted skirts that visibly differ from the T-90SM.
ownerDecision.roofRevision: Owner requested 14 national variants including Hetman II and Zubr II, with different roof weapons, paired mantlet lamps, optics, eye/monocle housings and roof equipment. Measurements below include the new stations; primary hulls, fenders and turrets are retained.

ua_t72b3m_hetman_ii.silhouette: Ukrainian T-72B3M command modernization carrying the T-72B3M (2016) turret with its own frontal package instead of Relikt: a stepped prow of three raked courses of deep discrete ERA blocks on two facets a side, each set back as it rises, the blocks in open joints on short gunmetal ledges, dividers and a cheek frame post, with stacked jaw collars round the mantlet, shoulder returns and a roof course of three swept wedge blocks a side on a gunmetal sill rail; squared flank armour cabinets with two wall courses and a lid course of chamfered ERA cassettes, an open command basket behind the bustle with slat walls, a rear cable drum and stowage, wider cage wings on the cabinet lids, slit lamps, twin sensor heads, a scanner, two panoramas, red infrared dazzler pods, the 30 mm wedge station on the commander's cupola and its own field net. The native T-72B3M hull carries a framed chevron glacis of three sawtooth bands a side laid as shingled wedge blocks on gunmetal retainer ribs and joint cleats, a nose sill with two three-segment LED bars in proud visored armoured lamp boxes, three hinged two-tier lower-plate aprons a side, two-layer bow modules, heavy fitted skirts, joint caps and camouflage carriers.

pl_t72b3_zubr_ii.silhouette: Polish T-72B3 heavy modernization carrying the T-72B3M (2016) turret: raked cheek boxes faced by a flush grid of square two-layer ERAWA-2 pillow cassettes in the Zubr's Krata frame of bars and mullions funnelling into the mantlet, framed two-layer cassettes on the box lids and a four-tile roof grid, every cassette over a gunmetal bay floor, long squared armour cabinets behind three courses of the same cassettes, square lamps on the cabinet fronts, a long open slatted bustle basket with strapped packs and a roll, guarded rear lights, an independent guarded sight, a monocle sensor and split-panel roof sensor, the 12.7 mm WKM-B closed armoured casemate emplacement with its sensor head and a fitted feed bin carrying its boresighted searchlight, and its own field suit. The native T-72B3 hull carries three stepped glacis terraces between two LED cluster housings, each carrying one row of large two-layer cassettes between Krata mullions, framed lower-plate fields and deep four-course ERAWA skirts with a fitted front grid.

ownerAmendments.request: Lower all fourteen national variant turrets to reduce the exposed cylinder between hull and turret. Preserve the other new designs and roof equipment.
